walkthroughs.body_html:
The SI system rests on 7 base units:

- metre (m) — length
- kilogram (kg) — mass
- second (s) — time
- ampere (A) — current
- kelvin (K) — temperature
- mole (mol) — amount
- candela (cd) — luminous intensity

Redefined 2019: each tied to a fundamental constant (e.g. kg via Planck's h).

From base units we build others:

- Force: N = kg m s⁻².
- Energy: J = N m = kg m² s⁻².
- Power: W = J/s = kg m² s⁻³.
- Pressure: Pa = N/m² = kg m⁻¹ s⁻².
- Electric potential: V = J/C = kg m² s⁻³ A⁻¹.

Coherent: no conversion factors needed.

Standard SI prefixes:

- pico (p) 10⁻¹², nano (n) 10⁻⁹, micro (μ) 10⁻⁶, milli (m) 10⁻³.
- kilo (k) 10³, mega (M) 10⁶, giga (G) 10⁹, tera (T) 10¹².

1 GW (power station) = 10⁹ W; 1 nm (atom) = 10⁻⁹ m.

Dimensional analysis: check each side has same units to validate equations.

mcqs.q: Which is an SI base unit?
What does the spacing of field lines on a diagram indicate?
options: The strength of the field — closer lines mean a stronger field.
About 6 billion years, the same as the Earth.
Field lines are equally important regardless of spacing — only the arrows matter.
Wider spacing means a stronger field because the lines have more room to act.

mcqs.q: Why do transformers only work with alternating current?
options: Wider spacing means a stronger field because the lines have more room to act.
Transformers work with DC too, just less efficiently.
DC cannot enter a transformer because the iron core blocks it.
A transformer needs a changing magnetic flux in the core; DC produces a steady flux and so no emf is induced in the secondary.

mcqs.q: What is the currently accepted age of the universe?
options: Wider spacing means a stronger field because the lines have more room to act.
About 14 billion years — close enough for any purpose.
About 6 billion years, the same as the Earth.
